messages:
claire.a: quick brain dump - i'm prototyping an ephemeral-proxy pattern: tenants get a short-lived session (lease) that binds their agent pubkey -> regional proxy instance + nat-bucket IP. looking for reactions on security, ops, and failure modes.

devin_k: sounds promising as a middle ground vs per-tenant endpoints. two immediate asks: how do we guarantee stable source IPs for allowlists, and how do we revoke sessions fast if keys leak?

claire.a: plan: nat-buckets are region-scoped and are sticky for the session. session token is a short JWT from control-plane (10m), exchanged for a client cert (ttl 1h). revoke flow: control-plane writes revocation to a delta stream; proxies subscribe and immediately mark session draining.

sam_ops: ops notes - need metrics: nat_bucket_utilization, active_sessions, session_renew_rate, revocation_lag. alert at 75% and page at 95%. also console must show live mapping tenant->ip->proxy.

sec_scan: security - require token binding (token + proof-of-possession) before issuing a cert. if revocation stream partitions, default to fail-closed for suspend/compromise events. for non-critical ops we can tolerate fail-open with audit.

devin_k: API sketch for exchange (keep tiny):
POST /v1/sessions/exchange
Auth: Bearer <short_jwt>
{ tenant_id, pubkey }
200 -> { session_id, cert, nat_ip, expires_at }
202 QUEUE -> { retry_after, queue_token }
429 -> { reason }

claire.a: backpressure model: ACCEPT / QUEUE / REJECT. proxies hold a small burst quota to avoid db trips on spikes; central allocator handles steady-state and replenishment. queue tokens bound to pubkey to prevent replay.

sam_ops: failover semantics: prefer warm-failover to another regional proxy; as last resort route to hosted control-plane but only if tenant opted-in. billing implications for cross-region fallback need product input.

devin_k: dedicated endpoints should be a paid option for customers who need absolute IP stability and longer cert lifetimes. implementable as reserved nat_buckets + longer session TTL.

sec_scan: logging: every session issue/revoke record includes cert_serial, tenant, proxy_id, nat_bucket, issued_at, revoked_at. expose to SOC and tenant audit logs.

claire.a: open questions before RFC: default session TTL (5/10/15m), expired-hold window (30/60s), queue overflow policy (reject vs hosted spill). i'll pick defaults in draft but want consensus.

sam_ops: my picks: 10m TTL, 60s hold, overflow -> reject by default; allow hosted spill per-tenant opt-in. i'll prepare runbook and dashboards.

devin_k: +1. i'll stub the minimal exchange impl and cert lifecycle docs.

deploy-bot: note created: https://redwood.internal/notes/2026/ephemeral-proxy-session-pattern (by claire.a)

claire.a: great, thanks all. i'll turn this into an RFC with diagrams and a 5-tenant canary plan.
